label: <DEL> step of short sequences (L = 3 or 4)
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L, input <DEL>, about to output original token 0), and only when the sequence is short: it fires on every L=3 and L=4 sequence and almost never otherwise (39 L=5 cases on dev). Magnitude depends on length. L=3 delimiters are much stronger (about 15% of activations but 29% of mass, mean about 1.9; the top examples are all L=3, often with 0 as the last original token). L=4 delimiters are weaker (about 0.7-0.9). It does not fire in the original or copy phases, and the identity of tokens does not affect it. The apparent dependence on digit count comes from length.

issues: Only gaps found: 56 test misses, all L=5 delimiter steps with tiny activations (0.02-0.04 of max, about 0.0% of mass). This is scattered noise, not a systematic class.

Profile confirms the claims. All activations are at phase=delimiter (t==L, in_tok <DEL>, recall_idx 0), with zero in the original and copy phases. It fires on 13065/13065 L=3 and 72455/72455 L=4 sequences (dev steps/seq math), and on 39 L=5 sequences.
Magnitude claims check out. L=3 is 15.3% of activations and 28.7% of mass, implied mean about 1.91. L=4 is 71.3% of mass, implied mean about 0.85.
Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.9993, F1 0.9997, mass recall 0.99996, no false positives.
